posts.text:
Own it!
⠀
⠀
Believe that this is already yours...
Say that this is already yours...
This is already yours...

I'm thrilled to announce that I left the job everyone once wanted, including me. I had to prepare almost a year to get this job.

But I am still celebrating this milestone because I learned that 
a prestigious title means nothing if it costs your peace of mind.

Believe me, sometimes less is more.
Let go, of what's dragging you back.

To everyone reading this:
The best part of your story hasn't been written yet.
& my DMs are always open for you.

Most people don't fail at the thing they're scared of.
They fail at starting it.
The hesitation kills them before the attempt ever does.

You know the moment I'm talking about.
Right when you're about to make the move.
Something inside whispers "not yet."

"Not ready."
"You'll look foolish."
And it sounds so reasonable.
Like you're just being smart.
Like you're protecting yourself.

But underneath, something darker:
The fear that you don't actually belong there.
That they'll see through you.
That everyone will watch you fall.

That voice inside isn't wisdom.
It's fear hijacking your best moments.

Here's what I've noticed about people who actually move:
They didn't wait to feel ready.
They didn't wait for the fear to disappear.
They just decided the risk of trying was smaller than the cost of waiting.

You've already done hard things.
Things you had no plan for.
Things that felt impossible walking in.

You changed jobs. Lost things. Pivoted. Faced uncertainty.
And you figured it out.
Every single time.
That's not luck. That's capability.

But stress makes us forget.
When your nervous system runs hot, your brain invents threats that don't exist.
Every opportunity looks like a trap.
Every move feels like a gamble.
Every risk feels like ruin.

Confidence isn't something you build.
It's something you remember.
It's knowing you can adapt when things fall apart.
When there's no plan.
When the ground shifts.

The real risk was never failure.
It was letting fear decide for you.

♻️ Repost if you needed this.
Follow me Raj Vaibhav for the truths that move you.

The bullies in this story were not children.
They were their parents.

An 11 year old girl in North Macedonia has Down syndrome.
A group of parents did not want their kids in her classroom.
They organized a boycott. 
Kept their own children home. 
Called her presence "obstruction."

She started the school term late. 
Attended some classes completely alone.

The country's president at the time heard about it.
He did not release a statement.
He showed up at her house, held her hand, and walked her into school himself.

Adults built the wall. Someone else chose to tear it down instead.

Have you ever stood up for someone who was being left out? 
Or wished someone had stood up for you?
What's your story?

Repost & Like if bullying should never be met with silence.
